quote: \begin{table}[htbp]\caption{Only one of the five families takes the InfoLogger road.}\label{tab:sources}
problem: The table lists six sources, because the run orchestrator log is not one of the five worker families, so the caption and the body sentence disagree with what a reader counts.
fix: Only one of these six sources takes the InfoLogger road, and the run orchestrator log reaches no collector.

quote: Each collector tails only its own machine's directory, or each file lands once per machine.
problem: The consequence is inverted, because "lands once per machine" sounds correct while it means every machine indexes every file, so the reader misses why the rule exists.
fix: Each collector tails only its own machine's directory. A tail over the whole disk would make every machine index every file.

quote: We dropped its queue on the numbers in Section~\ref{sec:eval-kafka}, and the aggregator the queue fed, because the collectors feed the live lane directly.
problem: The live lane is the reason a whole part of the 2025 design was dropped, and it is defined only two pages later.
fix: ...because the collectors feed the live lane, the second copy of every record that leaves a worker, directly.

quote: Only one of the five families takes the InfoLogger road.
problem: The table lists six rows and nothing marks the run orchestrator log as outside the five, so the reader's count never matches the prose.
fix: Caption: "Only one of a worker's five families takes the InfoLogger road." Set the last row's tier cell to "None, and not a worker family".

quote: It runs on five staging machines, and one farm deployment passed every check.
problem: The farm pilot ran the cluster, the collectors and Dashboards only, so page one claims more maturity than Section 6.3 allows.
fix: It runs on five staging machines, and one farm deployment of the cluster, the collectors and Dashboards passed every check. Make the same change in the abstract and the conclusion.

quote: A worker holds five log families, and InfoLogger is one of them (Table~\ref{tab:sources}).
problem: Table 1 carries six rows, because the run orchestrator log is listed although it sits on the shared infra machine and is not collected.
fix: Caption Table 1 "Five families reach a worker's collector. The sixth row is written on the shared infra machine and is not collected."

quote: Each collector tails only its own machine's directory, or each file lands once per machine.
problem: "or" plus the present indicative turns the bad outcome into a second available design, so the reader concludes duplication is an option rather than a fault being avoided.
fix: Each collector tails only its own machine's directory. If a collector tailed the whole disk, every machine collects every file.

quote: We built \loggy{}, a platform that keeps the bulk of the logs on the worker that wrote them and still searches them as one.
problem: "Worker" appears 73 times across the eight parts and no sentence ever says it is an Event Processing Node.
fix: We built \loggy{}, a platform that keeps the bulk of the logs on the worker, the EPN that wrote them, and still searches them as one.

quote: Its job is timeframe reconstruction: it assembles the detector data of one time slice into events.
problem: The introduction uses "detector" in its ALICE sense and Section 3.6 redefines the same word as a Random Cut Forest model, so "Seventeen detectors run" collides with the meaning a CERN reader already holds.
fix: Write "it assembles the data of one time slice from the experiment into events", and keep "detector" for the Random Cut Forest models everywhere after that.

quote: Only one of the five families takes the InfoLogger road.
problem: The table under this caption has six rows and nothing says the run orchestrator log is the row a worker does not hold, so the caption's count reads as wrong on sight.
fix: Only one of the five families a worker holds takes the InfoLogger road, and the run orchestrator log is not on a worker at all.

quote: The archive we replay is recorded farm logs, fed back through the collector at a chosen rate.
problem: "The archive" means the replayed stored logs here, the six months of dumps at line 42, the mined corpora at 02-design-a.tex:71 and the searched indices at 03-design-b.tex:31, so one word carries four referents.
fix: The stored logs we replay are recorded farm logs, fed back through the collector at a chosen rate. Then use "the InfoLogger archive" for the six months of dumps, "the parser corpus" for the 45,596,613 lines, and "the indices" where Discover is meant.
